item.title: Ben Crump’s Courtroom Doc Earns Emmy Honor
item.description: Ben Crump, along with filmmakers Cameron S. Mitchell and Raji Ramanathan and director John Beder, won a regional Emmy for producing the short documentary "How to Sue the Klan", which tells the story of five Black women in Chattanooga who used the 1871 Ku Klux Klan Act to successfully sue the Ku Klux Klan in 1982. The post Ben Crump’s Courtroom Doc Earns Emmy Honor appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Maryland’s Van Hollen Leads Democrats Planning State of the Union Boycott
item.description: Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D) of Maryland will not attend President Donald Trump's upcoming State of the Union address, instead joining fellow Democrats at a protest rally on the National Mall near the U.S. Capitol to protest the president's policies. The post Maryland’s Van Hollen Leads Democrats Planning State of the Union Boycott appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Predatory Lenders Target Americans Struggling to Pay High Rent
item.description: Predatory lenders are targeting renters with misleading "rent now, pay later" options that extract additional fees and increase the risk of eviction, while evading state-enacted consumer protection laws. The post Predatory Lenders Target Americans Struggling to Pay High Rent appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: DUMAS: The Slow Strangulation of Black Business Opportunity
item.description: The 8(a) Business Development Program is a long-standing initiative designed to help small businesses owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals compete in federal contracting, but critics argue it is outdated, vulnerable to abuse, and legally fragile, and that the real question is whether policymakers will do the harder work of governing it effectively or use enforcement as a pretext for eliminating it. item.title: Prince Perp Walk? Andrew Arrested in Epstein Bombshell
item.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the former Prince Andrew, has been arrested by British police in connection with newly disclosed Epstein files, with Prime Minister Keir Starmer stating that no one is above the law. item.title: The $50,000 Barrier Facing D.C. Car Buyers
item.description: The average price of a new vehicle in the U.S. has risen to over $50,000, making car ownership a financial stretch for many, especially those in the District of Columbia, where the cost of ownership is even higher due to taxes and fees. The post The $50,000 Barrier Facing D.C. Car Buyers appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Onyx Impact’s $500,000 Campaign for the Future of Black News
item.description: Onyx Impact has pledged $500,000 to support Black print, broadcast, and digital media in an effort to strengthen African American media and promote truth and democracy. The post Onyx Impact’s $500,000 Campaign for the Future of Black News appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Washington National Opera Brings Treemonisha Center Stage
item.description: The Washington National Opera is presenting a newly commissioned adaptation of Scott Joplin's 1911 ragtime opera "Treemonisha" at Lisner Auditorium, which follows an educated freedwoman as she navigates the realities of post-Reconstruction and highlights the valuable foundation of education in American history. The post Washington National Opera Brings Treemonisha Center Stage appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: The U Street Corridor: Past Glory, Present-Day Questions
item.description: Black Neighbors of 1617 U Street, formed by residents in 2023, is pushing for affordable housing in the U Street NW neighborhood, which has seen gentrification and displacement of long-term residents, while also advocating for the Green New Deal for Housing Act to preserve affordable housing via social housing. The post The U Street Corridor: Past Glory, Present-Day Questions appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Emmet Cohen and Janelle Gill Named DCJF 2026 Artists-in-Residence
item.description: The DC Jazz Festival has named Emmet Cohen and Janelle Gill as its 2026 Artists-in-Residence who will host a year of performances, master classes, and creative collaborations throughout the city to celebrate jazz as a vibrant, evolving art form. The post Emmet Cohen and Janelle Gill Named DCJF 2026 Artists-in-Residence appeared first on The Washington Informer.
